doc.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Art Ensemble of Chicago, Robert Crowder and the St. Louis players
summary: He explains the Art Ensemble and Air formed after he left, and the St. Louis BAG musicians who joined later.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Art Ensemble of Chicago. Now before Don Moye, Famoudou, got into the group, Robert Crowder, the drummer...
Yeah...
…you haven't mentioned him, did you know Bob Crowder?
No. I don't remember hearing Robert with the group. When I heard it I was already in New York, and they had already established themselves with putting paint on their faces and everything.
Well did you guys meet? Did you talk? Was it just always musical?
No, because Lester came in afterwards. I had gone to New York.
OK.
The St. Louis crowd came in.
From BAG, Black Artists Group? Lester, Julius Hemphill...
Yeah, Baikida Carroll and also although he wasn't a part of it, David Sanborn was from St. Louis also. Julius was a genius but anyway we'll talk about that later, too.
So, you were still there, let's say, 1965, 1964. So Roscoe… …Delmark records, he's already starting to record. That's where I heard Robert Crowder and Roscoe Mitchell's quartet.
Okay.
Some of those early recordings.
Oh, okay.
And then Air with Threadgill, Steve McCall and Fred Hopkins.
Yeah, that was a great group.
So these were already in formation at this time before you left Chicago or not yet?
No, they hadn't formed. They formed once I got to New York and then they came to New York.
That's when they...
That's when they took off. They weren’t there, Art Ensemble wasn't there when I was there. It came after I left.
